questions.title: Which court, if any, will grant Christa Pike a stay on the day of her scheduled September 30, 2026 execution?
questions.background: Christa Pike is on Tennessee's death row for the 1995 killing of Colleen Slemmer.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth: Use the court's order or contemporaneous reporting to identify the court. Resolution Date: Resolve to the court that grants a stay of Pike's execution on September 30, 2026, before her scheduled execution time that day. Accepted Answer Format: Answer with its commonly used short name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-09-28 legal & clemency update 2 days before Christa Pike's scheduled 10:00 AM CT Sept 30 execution at Riverbend (AP/Guardian, BBC, USA Today, Nashville Banner, Memphis Flyer, Hindustan Times Sept 28): (1) Gov. Bill Lee officially announced Monday Sept 28 that he is denying clemency and will not intervene, closing the executive commutation/reprieve pathway; (2) USA Today confirms Pike's attorneys formally filed their U.S. Supreme Court stay-of-execution application on Sept 25—raising the novel Eighth Amendment question of whether severe psychological/mental suffering during execution can be considered—and Tennessee filed its formal opposition brief in the U.S. Supreme Court today Sept 28, putting briefing on track for a Sept 29-30 SCOTUS decision. Across all Sept 28 coverage, the U.S. Supreme Court is the ONLY court with an active pending stay application, while Memphis Flyer explicitly notes 'Only action by Gov. Bill Lee or a federal court can stop the execution' after the Tennessee Supreme Court's 23-page Sept 23 denial. Raising U.S. Supreme Court 0.40 -> 0.52 as the sole active briefed venue while obeying anti-overconfidence given the 6-3 Court's high bar for stays; trimming None 0.22 -> 0.15 because Gov. Lee clemency is eliminated and Sept 26-28 passed without a pre-execution-day stay (while retaining 0.15 for execution without stay or a Sept 29 stay, mindful that 0/248 resolved market questions and 0/8 prior 'if any' questions resolved to None and resolution_criteria omits an 'or None' clause); trimming Sixth Circuit 0.16 -> 0.13 (no filing reported yet by Monday evening, though Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell can still file an emergency post-clemency-denial §2244 successive habeas or §1983 appeal on Sept 29-30 where Sixth Circuit panels are more stay-prone than SCOTUS); trimming Tennessee Supreme Court 0.11 -> 0.09 (Sept 23 denial final with no rehearing filed, though it retains exclusive state warrant jurisdiction over execution-day IV/thrombocytosis or female-team protocol emergencies); and replacing Davidson County Chancery Court (0.05) with Middle District of Tennessee (0.06), the Nashville federal trial court with direct §1983 TRO/stay jurisdiction over TDOC/Riverbend, leaving 0.05 residual for E.D. Tenn., Davidson County Chancery Court, and TN appellate/criminal courts.
